newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Embraer says in deal with Isreal's Elbit.
newsitem.headline: Embraer says in deal with Isreal's Elbit.

text.p: Brazilian aircraft maker Empresa Brasileira Aeronautica SA (Embraer) said it has picked Israel's Elbit Ltd to supply flight control instruments for at least 100 military attack planes.

An Embraer spokeswoman told Reuters the "mission avionics" will be used in its 500 million-real ($472-million) ALX Light Attack Aircraft Program being developed for the Brazilian air force. She declined to give a price tag for the Embraer-Elbit deal, which was signed last week but only made public Wednesday at the "Latin America Defentech '97" international weapons fair in Rio de Janeiro.
In a statement, Embraer said it chose Elbit over competitors after a selection process that gave "special attention given to local industries' participation and know-how transfer."

The contract calls for Elbit to supply an avionics suite that includes a modern central modular computer, colored liquid crystal and head-up displays, advanced navigational and weapons control systems and other features.

The ALX program calls for an initial 100 aircraft, advanced versions of Embraer's "Super Tucano," to be delivered to the Brazilian air force, known as the FAB, starting in 1999. "The 100 planes are for the FAB but they may be sold to third parties," the spokeswoman said.

According to Embraer, Elbit also supplies major aircraft manufacturers such as Lockheed Martin Corp, McDonnell Douglas Corp and Boeing Co and is involved in major aircraft upgrade programs in various countries.
